Reads at EVERY step (the bracket-tightest cadence). The arm is expected to resolve within a handful of steps (each step moves ~1.65 L2, so D=3.3 arrives by step ~2-4); the every-step cadence bounds the kill bracket at one step and the densification refines it WITHIN the step. Worst case (a direction stall keeping D below 3.3) is bounded by the 300-step cap at ~8-10 chunks.

Kill-bracket densification reads g-12 at parameter points theta_{s0} + f*(theta_{s1}-theta_{s0}) for f in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8} — points ON the same piecewise-linear parameter trajectory (between two committed training steps), not new training steps and not off-path probes; it refines D_kill's bracket only. Both the raw and densified brackets are reported; the window adjudication uses the densified bracket (frozen here before compute).
